title: Alibaba's Qwen Unveils Preview of Flagship AI Model That Rivals Anthropic
excerpt: The 2.4-trillion-parameter Qwen3.8-Max, which Alibaba claims is second only to Anthropic's Fable 5, sent the company's stock up 5.6% and signals an accelerating AI race between China and the U.S.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Max is a 2.4-trillion-parameter AI model, second to Anthropic's Fable 5.
  • The model will be open-weight, allowing free access for developers to modify it.
  • Alibaba's stock rose 5.6%, outperforming the Hang Seng Tech Index's 2.9% increase.
  • The release follows Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, escalating competition in the AI sector.

Wall Street Journal
  • Alibaba released a preview of Qwen3.8-Max, a 2.4-trillion-parameter flagship model it claims is second only to Anthropic's Fable 5.
  • The company plans to make Qwen3.8 open-weight, allowing developers to download and modify the model freely.
  • Alibaba's Hong Kong-listed shares rose as much as 5.6% on Monday, outperforming the broader Hang Seng Tech Index.
  • The release follows Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 launch, intensifying a rapid-fire AI competition between Chinese labs and U.S. frontier developers.

Alibaba Group on Sunday previewed Qwen3.8-Max, a 2.4-trillion-parameter large language model that the Hangzhou-based company describes as the most powerful in its lineup and second only to Anthropic's Fable 5 among frontier AI systems. The preview is available now across Alibaba's developer platforms, with an open-weight release planned in the near term, according to a post on X by Alibaba's Qwen team.

Investors responded swiftly. Alibaba's Hong Kong-listed stock climbed as much as 5.6% on Monday morning before settling at a 5.15% gain at midday, outpacing the Hang Seng Tech Index's 2.9% rise, according to the Wall Street Journal. Shares of smaller Chinese AI firms moved in the opposite direction: Z.AI, previously known as Zhipu AI, fell 13%, while MiniMax dropped 5.7% as the market priced in competitive pressure from the new release.

A Crowded Week for Chinese AI

"Open-weight releases let any developer run a model without paying the maker, directly pressuring the per-token pricing of American providers like OpenAI and Anthropic."

"Open-weight releases let any developer run a model without paying the maker, directly pressuring the per-token pricing of American providers like OpenAI and Anthropic."

Qwen3.8-Max arrives days after Beijing-based Moonshot AI launched Kimi K3, a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model that surprised Silicon Valley with benchmark scores trailing only Anthropic's Fable 5 and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 on certain evaluations. The Kimi K3 release triggered a semiconductor selloff on Friday that rippled into cryptocurrency markets, underscoring how sensitive global capital markets have become to shifts in AI capability.

Moonshot's momentum has been striking. The startup's annual recurring revenue reached $300 million in June, up from $200 million in April, and demand for K3 forced a temporary pause on new subscriptions over the weekend, according to CoinDesk. The company is now preparing a Hong Kong IPO within six months at a valuation that could exceed $30 billion.

"Competition is likely to intensify, eventually leaving only a small group of large language model developers capable of funding frontier-model development."

— Laila Khawaja, Research Director, Gavekal Technologies

Open Weights and the Pricing Pressure

Alibaba's decision to make Qwen3.8 open-weight marks a strategic divergence from its more recent proprietary releases. The company shipped Qwen3.6-Max-Preview in April as its first closed-weights flagship, a departure from the Qwen family's reputation as one of the most popular open-source model ecosystems on Hugging Face, where it has logged over 20 million downloads and 100,000 derivative models.

The return to open weights aligns Alibaba with a broader Chinese push to commoditize AI model access. Open-weight releases let any developer run a model without paying the maker, directly pressuring the per-token pricing of American providers like OpenAI and Anthropic. For Alibaba, the play is clear: drive adoption of the Qwen ecosystem and monetize through its cloud infrastructure rather than model licensing.

What It Means for India's Tech Sector

For Indian developers and startups, the proliferation of powerful open-weight models from China offers both opportunity and complexity. Open-weight access to frontier-class models lowers the barrier for AI-native products built in India, from enterprise automation to regional language applications. Indian cloud providers and AI startups that have built on the Qwen family can expect a performance leap once 3.8's weights become available.

But the geopolitical dimensions are unavoidable. India's technology policy increasingly scrutinizes foreign AI dependencies, and open-weight Chinese models occupy a peculiar space — technically accessible to anyone, yet originating from firms operating under Beijing's regulatory framework. Enterprise adoption may require careful due diligence on data handling and compliance.

Looking Ahead

The pace of releases signals that the AI frontier race between the U.S. and China is accelerating rather than stabilizing. Alphabet, Tesla, and Intel report earnings this week, offering the next read on whether Western AI capital spending is keeping pace with the competitive pressure from China's model labs. With Alibaba, Moonshot, and Z.AI all shipping trillion-parameter-class models within days of each other, analysts expect further consolidation — and further volatility in the stocks that have become proxies for AI's future.
